name: Atlas
description: A Rust inference server (binary: `spark`) built for single-box NVIDIA Grace-Blackwell hardware, with hand-written per-model CUDA kernels selected by a kernel target under kernels/<hw>/<model>/ rather than a generic compiler path. Its distinguishing features for the configuration space here are a first-class MTP speculative decoder with a width-adaptive draft-depth ladder, and Marconi-style checkpoint/restore of Mamba/GDN recurrent state (ssm_cache_slots) so hybrid SSM+attention models get prefix reuse that a KV-only prefix cache cannot give them. Serving configurations are published as YAML recipes in Atlas-Inf/sparkrun-recipes.

install.notes: The published GB10 image. It is a single moving `latest` tag, so pin the digest a run actually used — the version file for a run names it. Only aarch64/GB10 is published; there is no x86_64 image.

NCCL is a default cargo feature and libnccl is absent on a single-box DGX Spark, so the default feature set does not link. A source build must also carry the kernels/<hw>/<model> target for the checkpoint being served.

serve.notes: Two kinds of knob, and both are in the params list because both change numbers. FLAGS are clap arguments on `spark serve`. Booleans come in two shapes: plain switches (--speculative, --disable-thinking, --enable-prefix-caching) which are simply omitted when false, and tri-state Option<bool> knobs (--gdn-fused-norm, --ssm-batched-recurrent, --ssm-tail-midchunk, --prefill-varlen-batch, --disable-tool-grammar) which take an explicit value and whose absence means 'the engine decides', not false — which is why their registry default is null. ENV VARS are the second kind: several measured optimisations have no flag at all and are read from the process environment, so a recipe's documented ATLAS_* stack is part of the configuration and is registered here with the env var named in each param's help. The recipe YAML in sparkrun-recipes uses its own names for a few flags (max_model_len for --max-seq-len, host for --bind); those are in param_aliases.

notes: There are no releases or tags: Atlas ships as a rolling main plus a published container, so a version here is what the binary reports (`spark --version`), and the run's `engine.container` carries the image digest that produced it. Kernel targets are per model AND per hardware, so an Atlas build that serves one checkpoint on GB10 says nothing about another; `kernels/gb10/<model>/MODEL.toml` is what decides whether a checkpoint is servable at all.
